sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the south-western side of Roselle, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with Locust Street down the right margin and the avenues numbered West 1st to West 6th running across the sheet. A compass rose on the left shows north up and to the right. The densest building is in the eastern third of the sheet, between Pine Street and Locust Street, where the blocks numbered 9, 16, 17 and 24 are lined with detached frame dwellings facing West 3rd, West 4th and West 5th Avenues; the block at West 2nd Avenue and Locust Street holds the Second Baptist Church (Negro). Along West 1st Avenue at the top, houses stand on narrow lots on both sides, with the larger lots of block 1 above the avenue. Vine Street, drawn at an angle, runs from West 1st Avenue south-eastwards between rows of lots with dwellings along it. A trolley line with three tracks curves across the upper right of the sheet to West 1st Avenue and Locust Street, beside the Geo. A. Lutz Mfg. Co., makers of primary batteries, whose small works (heated by steam and lit by electricity, with a machine shop and an auto storage building) stands on Locust Street. The western half of the sheet is largely unbuilt, with large unsubdivided tracts (numbered 223 and 224) and streets marked only by their widths. At the lower left, Wheatsheaf Road crosses diagonally and a second West 5th Avenue, at an angle to the main grid, meets it, with a few houses beside them. A scale bar of 100 feet is printed along the bottom, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey appears at the very top edge. Sheet 3 lies to the right of the upper part and sheet 5 to the right of the lower part.
notes: Modern names: West 1st to West 4th Avenue are unchanged; the modern data names West 4th Avenue at Locust Street '4th Avenue' and West 5th Avenue at Pine Street '5th Avenue'.
Wheatsheaf Road and Vine Street survive under the same names.
West 6th Avenue is drawn curving at the bottom of the sheet; its junctions with Pine Street and Wheatsheaf Road lie 80 feet or more beyond the sheet edge.
West Roselle: Locust St to Vine St and Wheatsheaf Rd, W 1st to W 6th Av; mostly unbuilt west. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of the Borough of Roselle south of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. The sheet runs from Locust Street on the left to Chestnut Street on the right and from the railroad at the top down to West 3rd Avenue, taking in blocks 2, 7 and 10. Between the tracks and West 1st Avenue lies the town's business and yard strip: a large lumber and coal yard with lumber sheds, a coal shed on a planked siding, shingle and cord wood stacks and a wood sawing shed at its west end; a railroad ice house and the freight depot along the tracks; and the premises of W. D. Lewis Co., building contractors, with a woodworking shop, sheet metal work and storage, next to a public garage and repair shop for about twenty cars. A driveway runs behind these buildings. At the top right the passenger depot stands beside a small park laid out with a curving drive, and a tunnel is marked under the tracks. The blocks south of West 1st Avenue are lined with frame dwellings, with a few stores and flats near Chestnut Street. Block 10 holds the Borough Hall and the fire department on Chestnut Street, and the Roselle Casino with a lawn tennis court in the middle of the block towards West 3rd Avenue. Water pipes of six to twelve inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the corners. The blocks beyond Locust Street belong to sheet 2 and those beyond Chestnut Street to sheet 4.
notes: Locust and Chestnut are printed without a suffix; today they are Locust Street and Chestnut Street.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along the top of the sheet, with the passenger and freight depots.
Roselle centre: Locust St to Chestnut St, CRR of NJ to W 3rd Av; depots, Borough Hall, Roselle Casino. One part. Pilot.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the centre of Roselle east of Chestnut Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. It is the eastern neighbour of sheet 3: the Central Railroad of New Jersey fills the top of the sheet with its many tracks, and below them lies a strip of ground facing East 1st Avenue, including the passenger depot, which is stuccoed, and a small park with a driveway at the upper left. East 1st, East 2nd and East 3rd Avenues cross the sheet from Chestnut Street, down the left margin, to Walnut Street, down the right. The block between East 1st and East 2nd Avenues is the busier one: at the Chestnut Street corner stand the Van Court Inn, a hotel of 56 rooms heated by steam and lit by gas and electricity, with a city water connection, then a confectioner, the post office, a barber and the First National Bank, and the rest of the block is detached frame dwellings on deep lots. North of East 1st Avenue a battery factory, the Maxivolt Primary Battery Co., tenant of S. H. Howland (makers of miners' lamps), is drawn in pink with a note on its heating and lighting, among rows of dwellings. The block south of East 2nd Avenue has a row of small shops (a drug store, offices, a paint and wallpaper dealer and a tailor, in a building marked cement blocks) at its Chestnut Street end, an auto garage, and detached dwellings; the lower edge of the sheet is East 3rd Avenue. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are lettered in the avenues, with a fire alarm box at the upper left and a compass rose at the right.
notes: The modern names are East 1st Avenue, East 2nd Avenue, Chestnut Street and Walnut Street; East 3rd Avenue at Chestnut Street is a node named '3rd Avenue' in the modern data.
The sheet adjoins sheet 3 on the left, sheet 6 on the right, sheet 10 above and sheet 5 below.
Roselle centre east of Chestnut St to Walnut St, E 1st to E 3rd Av, CRR depot. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the southern part of the centre of Roselle, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Locust Street runs down the left edge, Chestnut Street down the middle and Walnut Street near the right edge, and the avenues numbered 3rd to 8th cross them, divided at Chestnut Street into west and east, with West 3rd to West 6th and East 3rd to East 8th Avenues lettered. The sheet has a compass rose at the right showing north up and to the right of the page. The blocks west of Chestnut Street (numbered 15, 18, 23 and 25) are residential, with detached frame dwellings along the avenues and the First Presbyterian Church on West 5th Avenue. East of Chestnut Street the blocks (14, 19, 22, 26) hold the First Baptist Church and St. Joseph's Roman Catholic Church on East 3rd Avenue, St. Joseph's Convent and Parochial School, and a larger Roselle school group drawn in pink in block 26: the High School and the Roselle Public School, both heated by steam. Dwellings thin out towards the south, where the large blocks between West 6th, East 7th and East 8th Avenues are marked as open or 'not open' ground with only a few buildings, and the blocks beside Walnut Street are lightly built with scattered houses. A scale bar is printed at the lower left in an unused block, with a small group of buildings drawn at its right edge. The sheet adjoins sheet 3 above, sheet 2 on the left, sheet 4 at the upper right and sheet 6 on the right.
notes: The modern data names these avenues West 3rd Avenue to West 7th Avenue and East 3rd Avenue to East 8th Avenue in places, and '3rd Avenue', '4th Avenue' and '5th Avenue' at their junctions with Chestnut and Locust Streets.
The blocks marked 'not open' south of West 6th Avenue are unbuilt streets as drawn.
Roselle south centre: Locust to Walnut St, W/E 3rd to E 8th Av; schools and churches. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern edge of the built-up area of Roselle, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, east of Walnut Street, which runs down the left margin. East 1st to East 6th Avenues cross the sheet, and a compass rose at the upper left shows north up. The streets of the eastern part do not follow a rectangular grid: Poplar Avenue and Chandler Avenue run down the sheet at a slant, and the blocks around them are wedge shaped, with East 4th Avenue and Mercer Avenue jogging where they cross. At the top, a strip above East 1st Avenue has dwellings along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which runs diagonally across the upper right with Hope Avenue beside it and a row of houses along its south side. Most of the sheet west of Poplar Avenue is residential, with detached dwellings on East 2nd and East 3rd Avenues, a few large estates, and the pink buildings of St. Luke's Episcopal Church, heated by hot water and lit by electricity, with its rectory beside it at East 4th Avenue and Walnut Street. East of Poplar Avenue the blocks (numbered 237 to 240 and 252 to 274) are mostly empty; Monroe Street and Adelphi Street at the top right and Stockton Avenue towards the bottom are laid out but with few houses, and Spruce Street runs down the lower left. The blocks along the lower edge (20, 21) are large and almost unbuilt. The sheet adjoins sheet 4 on the left above and sheet 5 on the left below.
notes: Modern names: Poplar Avenue is Poplar Street, and Monroe, Adelphi and Spruce are Monroe Street, Adelphi Street and Spruce Street; Hope Avenue, Chandler Avenue, Mercer Avenue and Stockton Avenue keep their names.

Two junctions on East 6th Avenue (with Chandler Avenue and with Poplar Avenue) lie 8 to 11 m from the modern nodes and were left out of the fit, as the old streets are drawn on a different alignment there.
East Roselle: Walnut St east to Monroe and Adelphi, E 1st to E 6th Av; fan-shaped streets east of Walnut (Poplar, Chandler). One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers a residential district in the east of the Borough of Roselle, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left: East 1st Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, East 2nd Avenue down its middle and East 3rd Avenue along its right edge, while Linden Road, Thompson Avenue, Sheridan Avenue, Drake Avenue and Harrison Avenue cross the sheet from top to bottom in that order. Linden Road runs at a slant across the upper part, and the short street Meadow leaves it northward at the top right. The district is thinly built: blocks 242 to 246 and 254 to 259 hold scattered frame dwellings, many with outbuildings, sheds, coops and private garages, and large parts of several blocks are still empty lots, above all block 246 at the top left. Public School No. 3 stands in block 258 on Linden Road, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, and the Wesley M.E. Church faces Sheridan Avenue in block 255, next to a small woodworking shop with an electric motor. Two buildings of flats stand on East 2nd Avenue in block 254, between Drake and Harrison Avenues. Water pipes of four and six inches are marked along most streets, with hydrants at several corners. The blocks along the left margin belong to the adjoining sheet 4, and those across East 3rd Avenue lie beyond the sheet. A scale of feet is printed in Drake Avenue.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the left (fitted rotation about -80 degrees).
Meadow is today Meadow Street.
Sheridan Avenue crosses East 3rd Avenue with an offset of about 34 m in OpenStreetMap; the eastern node was excluded because the sheet draws the street straight.
East Roselle: E 1st to E 3rd Av, Linden Rd to Harrison Av. Turned: north to the left. One part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the western part of the Borough of Roselle Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left. West Westfield Avenue runs down the right side of the sheet with the Central Railroad of New Jersey beyond it, and the Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the top towards the bottom right. West Webster Avenue, Seaton Avenue and West Clay Avenue run down the sheet roughly parallel to Westfield Avenue, and Laurel, Chester, Locust, Willow, Myrtle, Faitoute, Maplewood, Amsterdam, Oakwood and Williams Avenues cross them; West Webster Avenue divides around an oval park between Myrtle and Maplewood Avenues. Chestnut Place and Willow Place are short streets between West Clay and West Westfield Avenues, and Gordon and Hawthorne meet Westfield Avenue. The blocks west of the railroad are a thinly built residential district of frame dwellings with many vacant lots, with the Lincoln School in block 24. Along West Clay Avenue beside the tracks stands an electrical manufacturing works, and the strip along West Westfield Avenue holds stores, two hotels, the fire house of the Faitoute Hose Co. No. 3, the Church of the Assumption (Roman Catholic) and the Aldene M.E. Church. At the bottom right the plant of the Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. of America is drawn in outline, with its wireless tower, and a note refers to the enlarged drawing on sheet 13. The Standard Concrete Stone Co. occupies the top right corner.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the left (fitted rotation about -80 degrees).
Locust Avenue is today Roosevelt Street; Chestnut Place is Columbus Place; Willow Place is Chiego Place (identified from their positions against modern streets).
West Webster, West Clay and West Westfield Avenues are today Webster Avenue West, Clay Avenue West and Westfield Avenue West.
The Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. plant is drawn enlarged as an inset on sheet 13 (part 2), which is placed from building corners carried from this sheet.
West Roselle Park: W Webster, Seaton, W Clay, W Westfield Av, Lehigh Valley RR. Turned: north to the left. Old Locust Av = Roosevelt St, Chestnut Pl = Columbus Pl, Willow Pl = Chiego Pl. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the middle of the Borough of Roselle Park, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Four blocks (numbered 72, 73, 75 and 76) are laid out between West Grant Avenue along the top and West Westfield Avenue below them, with Locust Street on the left, Filbert along the middle and Chestnut Street down the right edge; Warren Avenue crosses the sheet between the two rows of blocks, and Butler Avenue and Charles and Williams Streets show only as stubs at the margins. The upper blocks are residential, with rows of frame dwellings facing Grant and Warren Avenues, small outbuildings and many empty lots in the interior. The lower block east of Filbert is the commercial edge of the borough: along West Westfield Avenue and at the corner of Chestnut Street stand a drug store, a bakery, a tailor, barber, plumber, cobbler and lunch room, a carriage room, wagon sheds and a blacksmith and wood-working shop. West of Filbert the lower block holds dwellings, a chicken barn and a general store at the Westfield Avenue corner, and the sheet's compass rose. South of West Westfield Avenue the ground is mostly open: a row of dwellings and tenements and a garage and oil company building stand west of the park, a small building and a driveway lie in the park itself, and the many tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey run along the bottom edge with a small waiting room at the lower right. Water pipes of 4 to 16 inches are marked in the streets, with dry hydrants and a fire alarm box at the Chestnut and Westfield corner. Adjoining sheets are 13 to the west, 10 to the east, 11 to the north and 3 to the south.
notes: Streets are listed in the modern data as West Grant Avenue, Warren Avenue, Westfield Avenue West, Locust Street, Filbert Street and Chestnut Street; no renaming was needed on this sheet.
The park south of West Westfield Avenue is unnamed on the sheet (lettered only as 'Park').
Roselle Park centre: Locust to Chestnut St, W Grant to W Westfield Av, depot park. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the eastern part of the centre of Roselle Park, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Chestnut Street runs down the left edge and Walnut Street down the right, with East Grant Avenue at the top and East Westfield Avenue near the bottom; the two streets in between, Charles and Williams, bend round the middle block, Williams turning from a north-south street into an east-west one that meets Chestnut Street. The blocks are numbered 91, 92, 93 and 94. The blocks along East Grant and East Westfield Avenues are residential, with detached frame dwellings on narrow lots. The middle block at Chestnut Street and Charles Street is the civic and commercial part of the borough: the Borough Hall and Fire Department (hollow tile, with a hose tower) stands on Chestnut Street, with grocery, hardware, plumbing, confectionery and tobacco stores, an agricultural implements and grain dealer, a machine shop, hay storage, a meat market and a dry goods store, and P. B. Polhemus's restaurant fixtures works. Below East Westfield Avenue lies the railroad depot park, with a curving drive, and a row of dwellings, a tile works and a garage face the avenue above the many tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which fill the bottom of the sheet. Water mains of 2 to 16 inches are lettered in the streets. The sheet adjoins 9 on the left, 12 on the right, 11 above and 4 below.
notes: Streets are listed in the modern data as East Grant Avenue, Charles Street, Williams Street, Westfield Avenue East, Chestnut Street and Walnut Street.
The vertical lettering 'Warren Av.' at the left margin continues the street that runs across sheet 9; it is not a street on this sheet.
Roselle Park centre east: Chestnut to Walnut St, E Grant to E Westfield Av; Borough Hall. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the northern and central part of the Borough of Roselle Park at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet has been placed with Locust Street at the left, Filbert Street, Donald Place, Lehigh Place and Chestnut Street across the middle and Walnut Street on the right; the cross streets run in pairs of west and east avenues, from Roselle Avenue at the top through Colfax, Lincoln, Webster and Clay Avenues to Grant Avenue at the bottom. Chestnut Street divides the west avenues from the east ones. The Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, passing Lincoln and Webster Avenues, with the passenger station and freight house on its south side at Chestnut Street. Most of the area is thinly built: the blocks (numbered 40 to 103) are largely empty, with scattered frame dwellings, and the houses concentrate in the blocks on either side of Chestnut Street between Webster and Grant Avenues and along the lower edge of the blocks facing Clay Avenue. Institutions are Livingston School No. 1 in block 83 (marked not in use), the Roselle Park High School, a large reinforced concrete school building in block 71 at the lower left, and the M. E. Church on East Grant Avenue at Chestnut Street. A compass rose near the right edge shows north pointing up and to the right, and the scale line at the top gives 100 feet to an inch. The sheet adjoins sheets 9 and 10 below and sheet 12 on the right.
notes: Modern names: Webster Avenue West and East Webster Avenue, Clay Avenue West and Clay Avenue East, Colfax Avenue West and East, Lincoln Avenue West and East, West Grant Avenue and East Grant Avenue, West Roselle Avenue and East Roselle Avenue.
Lehigh Place is identified as today's Park Place from its spacing west of Chestnut Street (about 260 feet on the sheet and on the ground); this was not confirmed against another sheet.
Walnut Street jogs at Colfax Avenue in the modern data (two nodes about 53 m apart) and the sheet draws it continuous; the junction was not detected and is not used as control.
The modern data has two Chestnut Street / Lincoln Avenue nodes 36 m apart (West and East); the sheet draws one crossing, and only the Lincoln Avenue West node was detected.
Roselle Park north: W/E Roselle Av to Grant Av, Locust to Walnut St, Lehigh Valley RR diagonal. Old Lehigh Pl = Park Place (continues the line of Donald Pl). One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the eastern residential district of the Borough of Roselle Park between East Webster Avenue and East Westfield Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left. East Webster Avenue runs along the left edge, East Clay Avenue and East Grant Avenue run down the sheet, and East Westfield Avenue runs down the right side with the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the far right edge. Hemlock, Spruce, Cherry, Birch and Walnut cross the lower left blocks; Magie Avenue, Avon, Berwyn, Camden and Dalton cross between East Grant and East Westfield Avenues; Union Road runs diagonally across the lower right towards Charles and Walnut; and in the upper part Sheridan, Sherman, Union and Madison Avenues run diagonally across the older grid. The district is almost entirely frame dwellings, densest in the regular blocks 110A to 110D between Magie Avenue and Dalton, with many vacant lots on the blocks west of East Grant Avenue. The Sherman School, built in 1912 of fireproof construction, stands on East Grant Avenue at Sherman Avenue, and the blocks across East Westfield Avenue are lined with dwellings backing on the railroad. Water pipes of six inches run in most streets.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the left (fitted rotation about -80 degrees).

Hemlock, Spruce, Cherry, Birch, Avon, Berwyn, Camden, Dalton, Charles and Walnut are printed without a suffix; today they are Hemlock Street, Spruce Street, Cherry Street, Birch Street, Avon Street, Berwyn Street, Camden Street, Dalton Street, Charles Street and Walnut Street.
East Clay and East Westfield Avenues are today Clay Avenue East and Westfield Avenue East.
Junctions of Sherman, Sheridan and Madison Avenues near East Grant Avenue lie 6 to 20 m from their modern positions and were not used.
East Roselle Park: E Webster to E Westfield Av. Turned: north to the left. Sherman/Sheridan/Madison junctions near E Grant Av 6-20 m off modern (rejected). One part.

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 covers the south-eastern corner of the Borough of Roselle Park, from East Grant Avenue down to East Westfield Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, and from Union Avenue east to Galloping Hill Road and the boundary of the City of Elizabeth, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Sheridan, Sherman and Union Avenues run diagonally down to East Westfield Avenue and are crossed by Madison Avenue; the blocks 116 to 118 between them hold frame dwellings on narrow lots. East of Sheridan Avenue the large block 122 is mostly open ground occupied by the slaughter house and stables of John C. Bender, wholesale butcher. Markthaler Place, Fernwood Terrace and Colonial Road lead off Galloping Hill Road, which runs along the right side of the part; Colonial Road curves south-west to East Westfield Avenue opposite Linden Road and is lined with small house lots in block 123. South of East Westfield Avenue a strip of stores and dwellings backs on the railroad, with the coal and masons' supply yard of David J. Farren and the mill, elevator and coal pockets of Aaron D. Crane. The boundary of the Borough of Roselle runs along the railroad at the bottom of the sheet. A scale of feet is printed in East Westfield Avenue.
notes: East Westfield Avenue is today Westfield Avenue East.
The junctions of East Grant Avenue with Sherman and Sheridan Avenues were hand-picked; the detector had placed them about 50 ft south along those streets.
Junctions on East Westfield Avenue were left out: the scale bar is printed in the street and the modern right-of-way is about 108 ft wide against about 60 ft drawn.

Three parts: 1 main (Roselle Park SE: Union Av to Galloping Hill Rd, E Grant to E Westfield Av, 100 ft); 2 inset top left (Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. works, 50 ft, placed from corners carried from sheet 8); 3 top right (Hawthorne to Locust, W Grant to W Westfield Av, 100 ft; old Pine = Meadow St).

sheet-13-2.description: An inset in the upper left corner of sheet 13, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up, gives an enlarged plan of the works of the Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. of America on the south side of West Westfield Avenue in Roselle Park, between the Lehigh Valley Railroad crossing at the upper left and the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the bottom. The main building is an L-shaped brick structure: a wing for glass blowing, testing, stock and packing with offices above, and a long wing for stock, a box shop, a machine shop and bench work, with a gas oven, all of concrete floor and with automatic sprinklers. Beside it stand a 20,000 gallon water tank elevated 60 feet, a coal house, a heating plant, an oil house, a shed and a separate laboratory, and the wireless tower, 215 feet high, stands near the street. A long note gives the fire protection of the plant: night and Sunday watchman, steam heat, electric light and power, the sprinkler system and its water supply, hose and fire pails. The adjoining blocks belong to sheet 8, where the same plant is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Placed from four corners of the main building carried from sheet 8 (no street junction is drawn on the inset); low confidence.
West Westfield Avenue is today Westfield Avenue West.

Three parts: 1 main (Roselle Park SE: Union Av to Galloping Hill Rd, E Grant to E Westfield Av, 100 ft); 2 inset top left (Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. works, 50 ft, placed from corners carried from sheet 8); 3 top right (Hawthorne to Locust, W Grant to W Westfield Av, 100 ft; old Pine = Meadow St).

sheet-13-3.description: The upper right part of sheet 13 covers a block of the Borough of Roselle Park between Hawthorne and Locust, from West Grant Avenue at the top down to West Westfield Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. Butler Avenue and Warren Avenue cross it, and Cedar and Pine run north from Warren Avenue to West Grant Avenue. Most of the area is still laid out in large undivided tracts (blocks 39B, 39C, 39E, 59 and 60); the only development is a row of frame dwellings and flats along Locust and a line of small houses on the north side of West Westfield Avenue in block 61. Between West Westfield Avenue and the railroad, block 22 holds a few dwellings and the yard of the Standard Concrete Stone Co. on a siding. Water pipes of six to sixteen inches run in the streets.
notes: Pine is today Meadow Street (identified by its spacing from Hawthorne and Locust); Cedar has no modern counterpart.
Hawthorne and Locust are today Hawthorne Street and Locust Street; West Westfield Avenue is Westfield Avenue West.

Three parts: 1 main (Roselle Park SE: Union Av to Galloping Hill Rd, E Grant to E Westfield Av, 100 ft); 2 inset top left (Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. works, 50 ft, placed from corners carried from sheet 8); 3 top right (Hawthorne to Locust, W Grant to W Westfield Av, 100 ft; old Pine = Meadow St).
